subjects.label: Creatures and taming
subjects.description: The dinosaurs and other creatures themselves: taming them, how the wild and tamed ones behave and whether they obey, being chased or eaten by them, and creatures that shrug off your weapons; not combat or crafting in general.

subjects.label: Remaster versus the original
subjects.description: Weighing this remaster against the game it remakes: whether it is better or worse than the original, missing the old engine, features removed in the reboot, and whether the original still gets the new content; not comparisons with unrelated games.

subjects.label: Which graphics card you need
subjects.description: Players naming the card or rig they own and whether it copes, the GPU tier they say you must have, and needing new hardware to play at all; not frame-rate complaints without a hardware frame of reference.

subjects.label: Install size and patch downloads
subjects.description: The footprint of the game, its maps, its updates and its dev kit on disk: patches of many gigabytes that take hours to install, running out of space, and updates for content you do not own; not what the patches change.

subjects.label: Official versus community servers
subjects.description: Choosing where to play: official servers against unofficial or boosted ones with custom rates and admins, self-hosted dedicated clusters, and adverts for a server; not lag, matchmaking or co-op in general.

subjects.label: Expansion maps and what they add
subjects.description: The named expansion maps and the headline additions they bring, such as trains, poker and mythological creatures, whether a map is free or paid, and whether the old game gets it too; not how much content the base game holds.

subjects.label: Time sink and compulsion
subjects.description: The game swallowing hundreds or thousands of hours and any life outside it, and the love-hate bond of hating it yet being unable to stop; not whether a single session feels immersive or atmospheric.
